chunks: I said to Zurara that Bukayr ibn A'yan narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
that the (legislated) shares of inheritance do not exceed (the total) and do not become more than six
So he (Zurara) said: This is something about which there is no disagreement among our companions, (transmitted) from Abu Abdillah and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them)

key_terms.اخْتِلَافٌ: Disagreement or ikhtilaf — here Zurara uses it to stress that this ruling has complete consensus (ijma') among Shia jurists.
key_terms.السِّهَامَ: The fixed shares of inheritance as defined in Quran 4:11-12 and 4:176 — designated fractions for specific heirs (e.g., 1/2, 1/4, 1/6, 1/3, 1/8, 2/3). The maximum number of distinct share types is six.
key_terms.تَعُولُ: 'Awl — the legal concept of proportional reduction of shares when their sum exceeds the total estate. Shia jurisprudence rejects 'awl; Sunni schools (except Ja'fari) permit it.

ai.seo_question: Do inheritance shares exceed six in Shia Islam? What is the Shia position on 'awl (excess shares) in inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith records 'Ali ibn Sa'id reporting to Zurara a ruling attributed to Imam al-Baqir stating that inheritance shares (sihام) do not cause 'awl (overflow beyond the total estate) and cannot exceed six. Zurara confirms this is an uncontested position among Shia scholars transmitted from both Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq. The hadith directly opposes the Sunni jurisprudential doctrine of 'awl, which was introduced under Caliph 'Umar and allows shares to be proportionally reduced when they exceed the total — a position rejected by Shia fiqh on the basis of Imam authority.
